    "printed_title": "43. 乐音和噪音　响度和音调",
    "start_page": 120,

    "exercise_count": 0,
    "prose": [
      {
        "kind": "p",
        "text": "We hear many different sounds every day.\nSinging, taut instrument strings, and whistles can give musical tones.\nExplosions and a running internal-combustion engine can give noise.\n\nHissing snakes and barking or howling dogs are further examples.\nOur vocal organs can make musical tones as well as noise.\nThis familiar contrast leads us to examine the vibrations.",
        "id": null,
        "label": null,
        "printed_page": 110,
        "source_refs": [
          "p0120#4"
        ],
        "source_text": "我们每天听到的声音是多种多样的。我们中的任何一个人都能区分所谓的乐音和噪音。歌声、乐器的绷紧的弦的响声、哨声等等属于前者；爆炸声、内燃机工作时的声音、蛇的咝咝声、狗的嗥吠声等等都是噪音。我们用自己的发音器官可以或多或少地发出一些和谐的声音，当然，也能发出噪音。",
        "changes": [
          "translation",
          "wording",
          "layout"
        ],
        "numeric_changes": [],
        "historical_entities": []
      },
      {
        "kind": "p",
        "text": "**Musical tones** How do musical tones differ physically from noise?\nWhy do different musical tones sound different?",
        "id": null,
        "label": null,
        "printed_page": 110,
        "source_refs": [
          "p0120#5"
        ],
        "source_text": "**乐音**　从物理学的角度去看，究竟乐音和噪音有什么区别？又是由于什么原因使各乐音彼此之间如此互不相似呢？",
        "changes": [
          "translation",
          "wording",
          "layout"
        ],
        "numeric_changes": [],
        "historical_entities": []
      },
      {
        "kind": "p",
        "text": "An almost pure tone can be made with a **tuning fork**.\nFigure 81 shows a fork fixed to a wooden box open at the top.\nA light hammer strikes one of its two arms.\n\nThe vibrating arms produce sound waves.\nTheir vibrations gradually die away.\nThe sound becomes quieter as the vibration amplitude falls.\n\nTo record the motion, attach a needle to one arm.\nLet it slide uniformly along a soot-blackened glass plate.\nIts vibration leaves a trace nearly shaped like a sine curve.\n\nFigure 82 shows this trace.\nUniform sliding spreads the motion out in time along the plate.\nThis is called a **time trace** of the vibration.\n\nIt resembles the pattern made with a sand pendulum.\nThe nearly sinusoidal trace shows nearly harmonic vibration.\nThis is how the tuning fork's motion is identified.",
        "id": null,
        "label": null,
        "printed_page": 110,
        "source_refs": [
          "p0120#6",
          "p0121#1",
          "p0121#4"
        ],
        "source_text": "纯粹的乐音可以使用叫作**音叉**的简单的仪器获得。图81所示的音叉是固定在一只上面开口的木盒上的。用小锤敲一下音叉的一个臂，我们就可以听到乐音。由于两个叉振动衰减，声音就逐渐减弱。声波是由音叉两臂的振动引起的。如果用一根针固定在音叉的一个臂上，使此针在烟熏过的玻璃板表面上匀速地滑动，就能确定这些振动的特征。在玻璃平板上会出现极近似于正弦曲线的线（图82）。这是振动的**时间展开图**，这种展开图与用沙摆获得的图纹相似。由此可以确定，音叉两臂的振动极近似于谐振动。",
        "changes": [
          "translation",
          "wording",
          "layout"
        ],
        "numeric_changes": [],
        "historical_entities": []
      },
      {
        "kind": "fig",
        "text": "",
        "id": "fig-81",
        "label": "图 81",
        "printed_page": 110,
        "source_refs": [
          "p0120#7"
        ],
        "source_text": "",
        "changes": [],
        "numeric_changes": [],
        "historical_entities": []
      },
      {
        "kind": "cap",
        "text": "Figure 81. A tuning fork fixed to a wooden box open at the top.",
        "id": null,
        "label": "图 81",
        "printed_page": 110,
        "source_refs": [
          "p0120#8"
        ],
        "source_text": "图81",
        "changes": [
          "translation",
          "wording",
          "layout"
        ],
        "numeric_changes": [],
        "historical_entities": []
      },
      {
        "kind": "fig",
        "text": "",
        "id": "fig-82",
        "label": "图 82",
        "printed_page": 111,
        "source_refs": [
          "p0121#2"
        ],
        "source_text": "",
        "changes": [],
        "numeric_changes": [],
        "historical_entities": []
      },
      {
        "kind": "cap",
        "text": "Figure 82. A nearly sinusoidal time trace of the tuning fork's vibration.",
        "id": null,
        "label": "图 82",
        "printed_page": 111,
        "source_refs": [
          "p0121#3"
        ],
        "source_text": "图82",
        "changes": [
          "translation",
          "wording",
          "layout"
        ],
        "numeric_changes": [],
        "historical_entities": []
      },
      {
        "kind": "p",
        "text": "**Pure tone** Sound from harmonic vibration is called a pure tone.\nThis ideal sound has a single frequency.\nA general musical tone may contain several related frequencies.",
        "id": null,
        "label": null,
        "printed_page": 111,
        "source_refs": [
          "p0121#5"
        ],
        "source_text": "**谐振动的物体发出来的声音称为纯乐音，或简称为纯音。**",
        "changes": [
          "translation",
          "wording",
          "layout"
        ],
        "numeric_changes": [],
        "historical_entities": []
      },
      {
        "kind": "p",
        "text": "We hear differences in both loudness and pitch.\nLoudness tells us how loud a sound seems, pitch how high it seems.",
        "id": null,
        "label": null,
        "printed_page": 111,
        "source_refs": [
          "p0121#6"
        ],
        "source_text": "乐音在我们听觉上有响度和音调的区别。",
        "changes": [
          "translation",
          "wording",
          "layout"
        ],
        "numeric_changes": [],
        "historical_entities": []
      },
      {
        "kind": "p",
        "text": "**Loudness** is how loud a sound seems to a listener.\nCompare the same fork at the same listening position.\nA harder strike makes the vibration amplitude larger.\n\nThe fork then generally sounds louder.\nThis comparison keeps the frequency and listening conditions the same.\nLoudness also depends on how the ear responds.",
        "id": null,
        "label": null,
        "printed_page": 111,
        "source_refs": [
          "p0121#7"
        ],
        "source_text": "**声音的响度**　声音的响度是由振幅决定的。小锤对音叉的打击越有力，音叉发声就越响亮。打击越强烈，引起振动的振幅越大。无疑，任何声音的响度都是由声波的振幅所决定的。",
        "changes": [
          "translation",
          "wording",
          "layout"
        ],
        "numeric_changes": [],
        "historical_entities": []
      },
      {
        "kind": "p",
        "text": "Our ears are not equally sensitive to all frequencies.\nEqual sound-wave amplitudes need not sound equally loud.\nChanging frequency can change the loudness we hear.\n\nThe source places greatest sensitivity near 3500 Hz.\nThis is an approximate description, not a fixed rule.\nSensitivity depends on the listener and sound level.",
        "id": null,
        "label": null,
        "printed_page": 111,
        "source_refs": [
          "p0121#8"
        ],
        "source_text": "但是应当指出，我们耳朵的灵敏度取决于声的频率。振幅相同的声振动，如果它们的频率不同，我们听起来就不是同样的响亮。我们的耳朵对于频率为3500赫兹左右的振动最敏感。",
        "changes": [
          "translation",
          "wording",
          "layout"
        ],
        "numeric_changes": [],
        "historical_entities": []
      },
      {
        "kind": "p",
        "text": "**Pitch** is how high or low a tone sounds.\nCompare tuning forks of different sizes.\nAttach a needle to an arm of each sounding fork.\n\nRecord each motion on soot-blackened glass.\nUse the same uniform sliding speed for each record.\nThe higher tone gives a sine-like trace with a shorter period.\n\nA shorter period means more vibrations in the same time.\nIts vibration frequency is therefore higher.\nFor a pure tone, frequency determines pitch.",
        "id": null,
        "label": null,
        "printed_page": 111,
        "source_refs": [
          "p0121#9"
        ],
        "source_text": "**音调**　为了判明一定的音调和什么有关，需要用几个大小不同的音叉。把针固定在发声音叉的一个臂上，并使针在烟熏过的板上划动，就可以发现，发音越高的音叉在玻璃板上划出的正弦曲线的周期就越短，因此，音叉的振动频率也就越大。**音调是由振动频率决定的。**",
        "changes": [
          "translation",
          "wording",
          "layout"
        ],
        "numeric_changes": [],
        "historical_entities": []
      },
      {
        "kind": "p",
        "text": "A vibrating string shows the same link to pitch.\nKeep the string and its vibrating length unchanged.\nIncreasing its tension raises its natural frequency.\n\nA guitar's tuning peg can tighten the string.\nThe tighter string vibrates faster.\nIt therefore produces a higher tone.",
        "id": null,
        "label": null,
        "printed_page": 111,
        "source_refs": [
          "p0121#10",
          "p0122#1"
        ],
        "source_text": "弦振动时，也可以观察到同样的现象。弦的张力增大就导致自由振动的频率增加。所以用小栓拉紧吉他的弦，就能奏出较高的音来。",
        "changes": [
          "translation",
          "wording",
          "layout"
        ],
        "numeric_changes": [],
        "historical_entities": []
      },
      {
        "kind": "p",
        "text": "**Noise** Typical noise mixes many frequencies irregularly.\nIt has no single stable pitch.\nMusical tones can also mix frequencies, in a repeating pattern.\n\nSuch a pattern can give a definite pitch.\nSome real sounds combine a tone with noise.\nThe distinction is not simply loud versus quiet.",
        "id": null,
        "label": null,
        "printed_page": 112,
        "source_refs": [
          "p0122#2"
        ],
        "source_text": "**什么是噪音？**　噪音和乐音的区别在于噪音不对应任何一个确定的振动频率，因此，也没有固定的音调。在噪音里，各种各样频率的振动混杂在一起。",
        "changes": [
          "translation",
          "wording",
          "layout"
        ],
        "numeric_changes": [],
        "historical_entities": []
      }
    ],
